model: Mars-van Krevelen site balance at steady state: two half-reactions, one common vacancy variable, one crossing
scope: Steady-state Mars-van Krevelen redox of an oxygen carrier under simultaneous exposure to a reductant and an oxidant. Nothing adsorbs and there are no surface intermediates: the two steps are written straight onto the lattice-oxygen site balance. The solid is described by ONE number, theta, the vacancy fraction on the two-coordinate bridging oxygen rows of rutile (110) - the site the descriptor is referenced to and the site the face ceiling comes from. Three-coordinate in-plane oxygen is not counted. The steady state is the crossing of the two half-reaction rates. This is the uniform-particle model: theta is taken to be the same on the reacting surface as in the particle average. That assumption is the model's largest declared error and solidgas/redox.py measures it rather than hiding it (see surface_correction). The reductant and the oxidant are deliberately unnamed: the rate parameters below are identical placeholders for both halves, so naming a gas pair would assert chemistry they do not carry. What the model requires of the pair is unit order in gas and in site.

reduction.label: assumed
reduction.note: Rate per oxygen site, r = A p^m (1-theta)^n exp(-E/kT). The site order n multiplies the AVAILABLE lattice oxygen, so the extent of reduction enters the rate as a factor and not as a shifted baseline. E rises with the descriptor: an oxide that holds its oxygen tightly is slow to reduce.

oxidation.label: assumed
oxidation.note: Rate per oxygen site, r = A p^m theta^n exp(-E/kT). E falls with the descriptor: a vacancy in a hard-to-reduce oxide is unstable and refills easily. The opposed signs of the two bep_slope entries are what makes the pair a volcano rather than a monotone ranking.

descriptor.name: surface oxygen vacancy formation energy
descriptor.reference_material: rutile TiO2 (110) bridging O, sX hybrid
descriptor.reference_provenance: Li, Guo & Robertson, J. Phys. Chem. C 119 (2015), DOI 10.1021/acs.jpcc.5b02430.
descriptor.label: literature (reference), assumed (range and slopes)
descriptor.note: The model is driven by the OFFSET from the reference, not by the absolute value, because only differences enter the two barriers. The absolute scale is quoted for orientation and is strongly functional dependent: the same authors report 4.39 eV with sX and 3.71 eV with GGA for the same site, a 0.68 eV spread. That spread is the systematic uncertainty on placing a material along this axis, and it is comparable to the width of the volcano itself, so a computed E_vac alone does not rank two materials that sit within ~0.7 eV of each other.

structure.label: estimate
structure.note: Point-defect solubility of the reduced solid, x in MO(2-x). Above it the vacancies stop being independent point defects: rutile orders them into crystallographic shear planes (Magneli Ti(n)O(2n-1)), so theta is no longer a mass-action concentration and this rate model leaves its domain. theta_solubility = x_solubility / oxygen_per_formula. The default is the rutile estimate carried in data/rutile_dft.json; a fluorite oxide holds a far wider single-phase range and would be entered here as its own value. This one number is what separates a carrier that can sit at its kinetic optimum from one that must change phase to get there. theta on the particle is stoichiometric bookkeeping, x/2 in MO(2-x), and says nothing about which defect holds the reduction: in rutile at low x the majority point defect is the titanium interstitial, not the oxygen vacancy.

regime_thresholds.note: Reporting bands only, not physics: below theta_lo the crossing is set by the reduction step and the solid stays oxidised; above theta_hi it is set by the oxidation step and the solid stays reduced.
